exposure: history of obstetric anal sphincter injury (OASI)
cohort: 2272 primiparous women who sustained an obstetric anal sphincter injury (OASI) during a singleton, term, cephalic, vaginal delivery between 2004 and 2015 and had a subsequent delivery
finding: Increased birth weight, maternal age at both index and subsequent deliveries, a more severe degree of initial OASI, and Asian ethnicity were associated with an increased risk of rOASI, while mediolateral episiotomy significantly reduced the risk.
mod_finding: Women with a history of obstetric anal sphincter injury (OASI) who had a mediolateral episiotomy (MLE) had a decreased risk of OASI recurrence at subsequent vaginal delivery.
